thread:
julia: Dropped a new "spend matrix" mock in Figma — compact card grid grouped by billing cluster (org vs project). Link: https://figma.com/file/spend-matrix-2026 99Can everyone weigh in on invoice discoverability + admin vs viewer visibility?

omar: Nice. First thought: clusters help finance scan by cost center. For invoices, should we show per-cluster quick-download or keep a single org-level download?

ben: For power users, quick-download per cluster is great. For watchers/viewers, we might hide download controls to avoid accidental exports. We should respect role perms in the UI: show buttons only to Billing Admins.

nina: Accessibility note: if we hide controls by role, ensure keyboard users don't land on hidden controls. Use aria-hidden when controls aren't present and remove from tab order. Also announce when actions are unavailable: e.g., a small helper text "Only Billing admins can download invoices."

a11y-bot: Contrast: the tiny chip text on the matrix uses #b6c7ff which fails AA for 12px. Suggest #5f7be6. Also if the matrix is navigable as a grid, implement role="grid" semantics and roving tabindex for arrow-key navigation.

julia: Good catch on color. I'll update the swatches. Thinking of adding a floating action button (FAB) anchored bottom-right for bulk "Download selected invoices (CSV)" when user enters select mode. That keeps the matrix clean and surfaces bulk actions.

omar: FAB is good on desktop and mobile but must be contextual. If user selects zero items, FAB should show "Select items to download" tooltip or be disabled. Also we need a confirm modal for large exports (>50 items) to explain async processing.

ben: Backend note: for >50 workspaces we should enqueue an async export and email the user a link when ready. For small exports do immediate CSV generation. infra-bot: what's the job cost?

infra-bot: Async export job estimates: 0.5s per workspace for CSV generation in current env; recommend chunking and rate-limiting. Also recommend gzip CSVs for large exports.

nina: Copy suggestion for FAB disabled state: "Select workspaces to enable bulk download". For accessibility, ensure FAB has aria-label and visible focus ring. Also provide a keyboard shortcut to toggle select mode (e.g., press D).

julia: Nice. Also debating inline token-breakdown: small inline percent + hover for absolute tokens vs always-visible numbers. For dense matrix, percent helps save space but hides scale. Maybe show percent inline and include a tiny "i" button to expand exact counts.

omar: Agree. Expand control should be accessible on tap/click and open a small popover with exact counts + link to usage detail. Popover must trap focus and be dismissible with Esc.

ben: Perf note: rendering mini stacked bars for every tile caused jank in stress test. Proposed approach: precompute rasterized microcharts server-side (8x32 PNGs) and serve low-res images; client can swap to higher-res on hover.

a11y-bot: Tooltip/popover accessibility checklist: role="dialog" or role="tooltip" as appropriate, aria-describedby on trigger, restore focus on close, ensure mobile tap dismissal.

julia: I'll update Figma with: 1) updated color tokens, 2) FAB disabled state copy, 3) per-cluster overflow menu for quick-download (visible to Billing Admins), 4) percent-first token pill + expand chevron.

omar: UX copy tweak for overflow menu: use "Download latest invoice (CSV)" and show file size estimate if available. Also add "Request export" if user is not allowed to download but can request one from Admins.

ben: Small naming nit for CSV: include scope in filename: redwood-invoices_org-<org>_2026-03-01_2026-03-31.csv so users can identify files later.

nina: Accessibility small: when scope switches (org <-> project), announce change with aria-live polite and keep focus on the scope control so keyboard users don't lose context.

julia: Action items: I'll iterate mocks with these changes and add component-level copy for aria-labels. @ben please add the async export RFC with cost estimates; @infra-bot can you confirm gzip/size limits? We'll review in tomorrow's design crit. :rocket:
